maya: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak last night we started seeing an uptick in KV cache misses + memory fragmentation on a subset of p99 workloads. Noticed sustained small OOM spikes on the GPU cache pool.

sam: Rough numbers? Which change exactly (kernel or batching)?

maya: Primary diff was: prefer fp16-fused matmul kernel for shorter sequences, and a new batching heuristic that pads to the next 16-token boundary instead of 8 (to reduce warp divergence). Both seem plausible.

maya: Profiling snippet from a repro run (50k requests):
```
hot_prefix_hitrate: 0.78 -> 0.61
avg_kv_entries_per_gpu: 220k -> 310k
fragmentation_ratio (slab): 0.12 -> 0.32
gpu_cache_alloc_failures: 12 -> 87 (window=1h)
avg_batch_fill: 0.83 -> 0.95
90th_lat_ms: 58 -> 63
```

li: Ouch. That fragmentation jump screams key duplication + variable-size allocations. Did the key canonicalization path change anywhere (prompt normalizer)?

maya: We hadn't touched canonicalization, but the batching change increased request coalescing which exposed lots of slightly-different prompt prefixes that used to be cold and now live concurrently. So the working set spiked.

toni: Hypothesis: more coalesced batches => more simultaneous KV insertions => increased allocation churn + more short-lived keys that displace slab buddies. Two mitigation angles: reduce churn (adaptive batching/contact windows) OR make eviction more locality-aware (per-slab LRU + compaction).

emma: For canonicalization we could normalise whitespace/punctuation and map templated tokens to a stable placeholder pre-insert. Example pseudocode: 
```python
def canonical_key(prompt):
    p = prompt.strip()
    p = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", p)
    p = re.sub(r"\{\{user_[0-9]+\}\}", "{{USER}}", p)
    return sha1(p)
```
That should collapse a lot of near-duplicates and reduce distinct key cardinality.

sam: Nice. Also consider a cheap semantic hash (first-N tokens normalized) so we don't over-collapse different intent. We want precision for QA prompts.

li: Agreed. Another idea: adaptive TTL per key using interarrival estimate. If t_last and t_prev are arrival times, use tau = median_i(delta_i) and set TTL = 2 * tau (clamped). This keeps hot streaks cached and lets ephemeral keys die quickly.

toni: TTL formula looks good. We should run that in shadow mode first. Implementation plan: shadow TTL calculation (no eviction changes), gather stats for 48h, then flip to enforce if hit-rate predicts >5% improvement without bumping memory pressure.

infra-bot: ALERT: 2026-03-16T03:12Z — detected GPU pool gpu-infer-11 allocation failures x93 in 1h; top culprit prefixes: ["order summary", "invoice preview", "chat.system_notice*"] (sampled).

maya: Thanks infra-bot — that sampling aligns with the 'templated tokens' hypothesis. I'll wire a canonicalizer for templated tokens and run a synthetic with the new batching heuristic.

sam: On the kernel side — the fp16 kernel path uses different scratch allocations that can increase transient memory. If we fall back to the previous kernel for sequences < 24 tokens (or when free_mem < threshold), that might reduce peak. Suggestation: kernel_selection: prefer_fp16 if seq >= 24 and free_mem > 1.2GB.

emma: We should also add a lightweight slab compaction hook that runs when fragmentation_ratio > 0.25: evict a small % of the oldest cold keys and defragment. This is cheaper than a full restart and avoids high-latency GC.

li: Add per-prefix crediting metrics so we can attribute which templates create most fragmentation. For sampling: 1/1000 requests record key size + slab id + residency_time. That should be low overhead.

sam: Proposed experiments (QA checklist):
- A: deploy canonicalizer (templated tokens) in shadow, collect delta cardinality for 24h.
- B: shadow TTL estimator for 48h, compute predicted hit-rate change and memory delta.
- C: kernel fallback rule (seq < 24 or free_mem low) behind toggle, run canary on 10% traffic.
- D: slab compaction hook with conservative thresholds on canary.
- E: change batching pad-from-16 back to 8 on canary to compare batch efficiency vs cache working set.

maya: I'll own A and E. Li will own B and per-prefix sampling. Toni + infra will own C and D. We'll reconvene in ~36h or when canaries report.

ops-bot: Runbook note added: "If gpu_cache_alloc_failures > 50 in 1h, mark canary false-positive and roll back kernel/batching toggle automatically."

sam: One extra caution: do not over-aggregate keys — keep an opt-out list for low-ambiguity prompts (payment, login flows). We'll white-list by route.

maya: Logged the rollout plan in the release board, kickstarting canaries now. Will post short repro when I have synthetic results. :chip: :spiral_calendar:

toni: Thanks — if the compaction hook proves useful we can backport to Dedicated pools too.

sam: Great, keep notes on hit-rate vs latency trade-offs. We're trying to avoid a fix that hurts p50 while improving hit-rate.

maya: Copy that. Starting shadow runs now.

emma: If anyone wants the profiling script I used to produce the snippet above ping me and I'll drop it in the thread.

maya: pinged emma for script :thumbsup:
